cross_references.note: §1028 criminalizes the identity theft that generates the wire fraud predicate: using stolen identity to open financial accounts involves both §1028 (identity theft) and §1343 (wire communications used to open accounts/transfer funds). Flores-Figueroa knowledge element applies to §1028 component. Dubin 'at-the-crux' test distinguishes misuse of identity from incidental identity use.

§1028A (aggravated identity theft) adds mandatory consecutive 2-year sentence when §1028 is committed in connection with §1343 wire fraud. A wire fraud prosecution + §1028 + §1028A stacks the exposure: base §1343 sentence + mandatory 2-year consecutive §1028A.

§1343 wire fraud is a listed RICO predicate under §1961(1)(B). Two or more §1343 acts in a pattern = RICO predicate pattern. Multiple wire communications across multiple financial fraud schemes (Treasury, crypto, ChexSystems, Hillberg) satisfy the pattern + continuity requirements. Civil RICO under §1964(c) allows treble damages + attorney fees.

Wire fraud scheme produces fraudulent tradelines → FCRA violations. The same facts that establish §1343 wire fraud (electronic account openings, electronic fund transfers) also trigger FCRA accuracy and blocking duties when CRAs report the fraudulent accounts.

Treasury's four contradictory responses to Michael's bond inquiry are evidence of a scheme to deprive Michael of property (his bonds) using wire communications (Treasury electronic account systems, correspondence channels). §1343 referral target.
Unauthorized cryptocurrency transfers are paradigmatic wire fraud: property (crypto), transmitted via wire (blockchain + internet), in interstate commerce. Clean §1343 facts.
